about.title: What is EUROXPRO?
about.description: The yearly regional conference of AIESEC in Europe.
paragraphs: **EUROXPRO** brings together national leadership teams (Member Committees), Local Committee presidents, functional vice presidents and alumni from more than 50 entities of **AIESEC in Europe**.

Most of the week is working time: functional tracks, plenaries and the conversations between them, where entities agree on how to grow exchange (*Global Volunteer, Global Talent, Global Teacher*) and support each other.
In 2027 **AIESEC in Türkiye** hosts in Antalya. The working theme is *“Where Europe Meets the Mediterranean.”*

attractions.title: Must-See Sights in Antalya
attractions.description: A curated selection of the most significant ancient, coastal, and cultural landmarks easily accessible to delegates.
attractions.notice: **Cultural Exploration Notice:** The landmarks, museums, and natural sites below are curated suggestions for delegates seeking to experience Antalya independently before, during leisure periods, or following the congress. They are not mandatory excursions or included activities within the official conference fee.

items.name: Kaleiçi (Historic Old Town & Roman Marina)
items.description: Antalya's ancient walled heart perched atop sea cliffs. Cobblestone alleyways lined with restored Ottoman mansions descend into the 2nd-century BC Roman harbor with traditional sailing boats.
items.tips: Walk through the marble arches of Hadrian's Gate and take the panoramic glass elevator down to the harbor.

items.name: Lower Düden Waterfalls (Aşağı Düden)
items.description: One of the Mediterranean's most dramatic natural sights: the Düden River cascades 40 meters straight over rocky cliffs directly into the turquoise Mediterranean sea.
items.tips: Visit the Düden Park clifftop promenade at sunset for breathtaking coastal photography and sea spray breezes.

items.name: Konyaaltı Coast & Taurus Mountains
items.description: A sweeping 7-kilometer Mediterranean pebble beach framed dramatically by the snow-capped Beydağları (Taurus) mountain range plunging directly into crystal azure waters.
items.tips: The pedestrian promenade features modern seaside cafes, cycling paths, and open-air seating for delegates.

items.name: Ancient Aspendos Amphitheater
items.description: Widely regarded as the best-preserved ancient Roman theater in the entire Mediterranean world, engineered with peerless acoustics that are still celebrated today.
items.tips: Stand at the center of the orchestra floor to test the whispering acoustics carrying up to the 41st tier.

items.name: Hadrian's Gate (Üçkapılar)
items.description: A triumphal triple-arched marble gateway constructed to honor Roman Emperor Hadrian's visit to Antalya. Deep ruts in the stone floor still bear the marks of ancient chariot wheels.
items.tips: The gate serves as the grand pedestrian threshold transitioning modern Antalya into historic Kaleiçi.

items.name: Antalya Archaeological Museum
items.description: One of Türkiye's premier antiquities museums, showcasing stunning classical Roman marble statues from Perge, monumental sarcophagi, and Bronze Age artifacts.
items.tips: Accessible via the heritage Nostalgic Tram terminus right across from Konyaaltı beach.

food.title: Flavours of the Turkish Riviera
food.description: Mediterranean flavors meet classical Anatolian culinary mastery. From citrus orchards to fresh harbor seafood, here is what delegates should sample.

items.name: Antalya-Style Piyaz
items.desc: A regional culinary masterpiece: tender white beans tossed with a rich dressing of crushed sesame tahini, lemon juice, garlic, vinegar, and boiled farm eggs.

items.name: Fresh Mediterranean Catch (Levrek & Çipura)
items.desc: Fresh sea bass or sea bream grilled over olive-wood coals, drizzled with local extra virgin olive oil and wild herbs.

items.name: Citrus Preserves & Bergamot Jam
items.desc: Antalya's citrus groves are legendary. Enjoy whole sweet orange, bitter orange, and bergamot jams served with morning cheeses.

items.name: Mediterranean Serpme Kahvaltı
items.desc: An elaborate coastal breakfast spread with goat cheeses, garden-grown tomatoes, cucumbers, fresh olives, honey, and hot Turkish tea.

items.name: Yanık Dondurma (Caramelized Goat Milk Ice Cream)
items.desc: A historic Antalya dessert made from goat milk subtly scorched during boiling to create a complex, smoky caramel note.

items.name: Turkish Tea & Coffee in the Roman Marina
items.desc: Sipping traditional tea in delicate tulip glasses overlooking fishing sloops and cliffs as Mediterranean twilight descends.

etiquette: Saying *“Afiyet olsun”* (Bon appétit) before or after sharing food is polite and appreciated.
Mediterranean hospitality is legendary: complimentary Turkish tea (çay) is customarily offered after meals.
Local olive oils, citrus, and fresh seafood are seasonal staples celebrated along the Mediterranean coast.
Tipping around 10% in sit-down restaurants is standard and polite practice.

hero.title: Frequently Asked Questions
hero.intro: Quick answers about getting to Antalya, where you will stay, visas, registration and life at the congress.

travel.title: Getting to Antalya
travel.intro: The three things every delegate asks first. Detailed guidance is in the Delegate Guide.

items.title: Antalya Airport (AYT)
items.text: Fly directly into **Antalya Airport (AYT)**, about 13 km from the city centre. Many European cities have direct flights, and Istanbul (IST and SAW) connects to Antalya several times an hour. The Organizing Committee will run a **Welcome Desk at arrivals on 31 March**. The AntRay tram, Havaş airport coaches and licensed taxis are also available.

items.title: Hotel & accommodation
items.text: All delegates stay at the **official congress resort in Antalya**, where plenaries and evening events take place. The resort name, room types and check-in details will be announced by the Organizing Committee. Check-in opens at 14:00 on arrival day and check-out is at 12:00 on departure day.

items.title: Visa & entry
items.text: Visa rules depend on your passport. Many European citizens can enter Türkiye **visa-free for short stays**, others can apply online for an **e-Visa** in a few minutes. Check the official portal before booking and make sure your passport is valid well beyond your travel dates.

items.question: How do I register for EUROXPRO'27?
items.answer: Registration details and the official registration link will be shared once confirmed by the Organizing Committee. Keep an eye on this website and our social media channels for the announcement.

items.question: What is the registration fee?
items.answer: The official registration fee has not yet been confirmed. It will be announced alongside the registration opening. The fee will typically cover congress sessions, accommodation, and included meals as specified in the official programme.

items.question: Is there a deadline for registration?
items.answer: Registration deadlines will be announced when the registration process opens. We recommend registering early as spaces are limited.

items.question: Can I cancel or transfer my registration?
items.answer: The cancellation and transfer policy will be shared when registration opens. Please contact the Organizing Committee at contact@euroxpro27.com for any specific queries.

items.question: Do I need a visa to enter Türkiye?
items.answer: Visa requirements depend on your nationality. Many European nationals can enter Türkiye visa-free or obtain a visa-on-arrival/e-Visa. Please check the official Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs website (mfa.gov.tr) or the official e-Visa portal (evisa.gov.tr) for the most up-to-date information for your specific passport. The Organizing Committee cannot provide legal visa advice.

items.question: How do I get from Antalya Airport (AYT) to the hotel?
items.answer: Antalya Airport (AYT) is located approximately 13 km from the central city and coastal resort zones. The Organizing Committee will operate an official Welcome Desk at AYT arrivals on 31 March to coordinate direct delegate transfers. Independent transfer options include the AntRay light rail tram, Havaş airport express coaches, and licensed metered taxis.

items.question: Which airport should I fly into?
items.answer: You should book your flights directly to Antalya Airport (AYT). AYT receives frequent direct flights from major European gateways as well as multiple hourly connections via Istanbul (IST and SAW) on Turkish Airlines and Pegasus.

items.question: What documents do I need to bring?
items.answer: You will need your valid passport (check expiry date — it should be valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates). Depending on your nationality, you may also need a printed or digital e-Visa. Bring your congress confirmation and any travel insurance documents.

items.question: Where will delegates be staying in Antalya?
items.answer: The official congress resort property in Antalya is currently undergoing contract finalization. Details including exact resort name, coastal location, room categories, and included amenities will be announced soon by the Organizing Committee.

items.question: Is accommodation included in the registration fee?
items.answer: Information about what is included in the registration fee (accommodation, meals, plenary access) will be confirmed when registration officially opens. This information will be clearly communicated before you register.

items.question: Can I arrange my own accommodation?
items.answer: We strongly recommend staying at the official congress resort to be close to all plenary sessions, evening socials, and fellow delegates. If you have specific needs or circumstances, please contact the OC directly.

items.question: How do I get around Antalya?
items.answer: Antalya has an efficient public transit network consisting of the AntRay light rail tram system (connecting the airport, bus terminal Otogar, and city center), municipal buses, and nostalgic tramway along Kaleiçi. You can use an AntalyaKart or contactless bank cards on AntRay and public buses.

items.question: What is an AntalyaKart?
items.answer: AntalyaKart is the rechargeable smart transit card used for all public transport across the Antalya metropolitan area. Contactless debit and credit cards (Visa/Mastercard) are also accepted on turnstiles and bus validators.

items.question: Will there be transfers between the hotel and venue?
items.answer: The congress plenary sessions and social evenings are planned within the integrated congress resort complex and designated cultural excursion sites. All scheduled group transfers will be fully arranged by the OC.

items.question: What currency is used in Türkiye?
items.answer: The official currency of Türkiye is the Turkish Lira (TRY / ₺). Contactless credit/debit cards are accepted almost everywhere in Antalya, but carrying a small amount of TRY cash is useful for small local purchases.

items.question: Can I pay by card in Antalya?
items.answer: Card payments are widely accepted across Antalya hotels, restaurants, transit, and supermarkets. Visa and Mastercard are the standard. Inform your bank before travelling to ensure your card is activated for international transactions.

items.question: Where can I exchange currency?
items.answer: Currency exchange offices (Döviz) are abundant throughout central Antalya and Kaleiçi. ATMs from reputable national banks (Garanti BBVA, İşbank, Akbank, Yapı Kredi) are also widely available and offer secure cash withdrawals in TRY.

items.question: What are the confirmed congress dates?
items.answer: EUROXPRO'27 is officially confirmed for 31 March – 4 April 2027 in Antalya, Türkiye.

items.question: When will the full agenda be published?
items.answer: The detailed agenda is coming soon. Session timings, workshop tracks and confirmed speakers will be published by the Organizing Committee on The Congress page and in Announcements closer to the event.

items.question: When will the merch collection be available?
items.answer: The official EUROXPRO'27 merch collection is currently in development. You can browse the planned Mediterranean collection and express your interest on the Merch Store page. Official ordering details will be announced separately.

items.question: Can I order merch before the congress?
items.answer: The ordering process is not yet open. Currently, the store is in preview/expression-of-interest mode only. No payments are being collected at this stage. Follow announcements for the official order launch.

items.question: Will merch be available at the congress?
items.answer: Yes, selected merchandise will be available for collection at the congress in Antalya. Details about ordering and collection will be confirmed by the Organizing Committee.

items.question: Are meals included?
items.answer: Information about included meals will be confirmed when registration opens. It will be clearly stated what is covered in your delegate package.

items.question: How do I communicate dietary restrictions?
items.answer: You will be asked about dietary requirements during the registration process. If you have specific allergies or dietary restrictions (halal, vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, etc.), please make sure to clearly indicate this during registration. The OC will do their best to accommodate requests.

items.question: Is food halal in Antalya?
items.answer: Halal food is the nationwide standard in Türkiye and is served across all congress venues and restaurants. Fresh vegetarian, vegan, and Mediterranean seafood options are also widely accessible.

items.question: What is the emergency number in Türkiye?
items.answer: The nationwide emergency number in Türkiye is 112. This unified hotline connects to police, ambulance, fire, and coast guard services. Calls are toll-free and English-speaking operators are available.

items.question: Is Antalya safe for international visitors?
items.answer: Antalya is one of the safest and most popular international resort destinations in the Mediterranean, hosting millions of global travelers annually. As with any international trip, standard precautions apply, and the OC will provide on-ground support throughout the event.

items.question: Who do I contact if I have an emergency during the congress?
items.answer: For emergencies, dial 112 immediately. The Organizing Committee will also operate a 24/7 on-call helpline for all delegates during the event, shared upon check-in.

items.question: Should I get travel insurance?
items.answer: Yes, travel medical insurance is strongly recommended for all international delegates traveling to Türkiye.

items.question: How do I contact the Organizing Committee?
items.answer: You can reach the Organizing Committee via the Contact page on this website or by emailing contact@euroxpro27.com. We aim to respond to all enquiries within 48-72 hours.

items.question: I didn't find my answer here. What should I do?
items.answer: If your question isn't answered in the FAQ, please use the contact form on the Contact page or send an email to contact@euroxpro27.com. We are happy to help with any questions you have.
